newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SmithBarney set $59 price for Ericsson, $114 Nokia.
newsitem.headline: SmithBarney set $59 price for Ericsson, $114 Nokia.

text.p: U.S. investment bank SmithBarney said on Wednesday it had set $59 as a target for shares in Swedish telecoms group Ericsson and $114 for Finnish rival Nokia, both over 18 months.
The bank has a buy recommendation on both shares, SmithBarney analyst Tony Langham told Reuters.
SmithBarney forecast profit per share of $1.30 for Ericsson
in 1997, $1.70 in 1998 and $2.20 in 1999, Langham said.
Average growth in earnings per share (EPS) was expected to be 27 percent annually between 1997 and 2001, he said.
Nokia's EPS was expected to be $3.82 in 1997, $4.70 in 1998 and $5.70 in 1999. Annual growth in EPS was seen at 21 percent each year between 1997-2001.
Ericsson's share was rising because of such a recommendation from SmithBarney, brokers said earlier on Wednesday. At 1250 Ericsson was trading 9.5 crowns higher at 301.5 crowns.
Nokia was trading in Helsinki at 390.50 markka, up 10.50.
